paras.text: When isomerism is caused by different arrangement of atoms or groups in space, the phenomenon is called stereoisomerism. Thus, the stereoisomers have the same molecular formula and connectivity of atoms, but differ in the arrangement of atoms or groups in space. In other words, the isomers that have the same constitution but differ in the spatial arrangement of their atoms are called stereoisomers. Some stereoisomers which are inter-convertible by rotation of single bond are called conformational isomers. But the stereoisomers which are not inter-convertible without breaking and making of some bonds, are called configurational isomers. Conformational isomerism is beyond the scope of this book, so we will discuss only the configurational isomerism in stereoisomers, which is of two types i.e. geometric and optical isomerism.

16.6.1.3 Functional group Isomerism

Functional group isomerism involves in compounds having the same formula but different functional groups. For example, ethyl alcohol and dimethyl ether are functional group isomers.

Similarly, Propionaldehyde and acetone are also functional group isomers.

16.6.1.4 Metamerism

This type of isomerism is exhibited due to the unequal distribution of carbon atoms (or alkyl groups) on either side of the functional group. Isomers belong to the same homologous series. For example, diethyl ether and methyl n-propyl ether are metamers.

16.6.1.5 Tautomerism

Tautomers are constitutional isomers that differ from each other by position of a proton (and may also a pi bond). It is a special type of functional group isomerism, in which the isomers are in dynamic equilibrium with each other. Tautomerization is the process of inter-conversion of tautomers, and an equilibrium process, which means that the equilibrium will establish with specific concentrations of tautomers of a compound. One of the important example of tautomerism is keto-enol tautomerism. The keto and enol tautomers of acetone are given below.

The result of this keto-enol tautomerization, is the migration of a proton from one location to another, accompanied by a change in location of the pi bond.

16.6.2 Stereoisomerism

When isomerism is caused by different arrangement of atoms or groups in space, the phenomenon is called stereoisomerism. Thus, the stereoisomers have the same molecular formula and connectivity of atoms, but differ in the arrangement of atoms or groups in space. In other words, the isomers that have the same constitution but differ in the spatial arrangement of their atoms are called stereoisomers. Some stereoisomers which are inter-convertible by rotation of single bond are called conformational isomers. But the stereoisomers which are not inter-convertible without breaking and making of some bonds, are called configurational isomers. Conformational isomerism is beyond the scope of this book, so we will discuss only the configurational isomerism in stereoisomers, which is of two types i.e. geometric and optical isomerism.

16.6.2.1 Geometrical Isomerism

Geometric isomers have different arrangement of atoms or groups when the rotation is restricted in a molecule. For example, but-2-ene have two stereoisomeric forms, cis-but-2-ene and trans-but-2-ene, as shown below.

The isomers in which the two methyl groups are on the same side of the double bond is called the cis (a Latin word meaning “on this side”) isomer, while trans (a Latin word meaning “across”) isomer has got them on the opposite sides of the double bond. Consequently this type of isomerism is also called cis-trans isomerism. Due to restricted rotation of carbon-carbon double bond, the cis and trans isomers are not inter-convertible without breaking of pi bond. These are two different compounds and have different properties.

Geometric isomerism in alkenes is possible only when each double bonded carbon atom is attached to two different atoms or groups, thus propene does not have geometric isomers. Geometric isomerism is also possible in substituted cycloalkanes. For example 1,2-dimethylcyclopropane also has two geometric isomers.

کله چې ایزومېریزم په فضا کې د اټومونو یا ګروپونو د بېلابېل ترتیب له امله وي، دې پدیدې ته سټیریوایزومېریزم ویل کېږي. نو سټیریوایزومرونه یو شان مالیکولي فورمول او د اټومونو نښلون لري، خو په فضا کې د اټومونو یا ګروپونو په ترتیب کې توپیر لري. په بل عبارت، هغه ایزومرونه چې یو شان جوړښت لري خو د اټومونو په فضايي ترتیب کې توپیر لري، سټیریوایزومرونه بلل کېږي. ځینې سټیریوایزومرونه چې د یو ګوني تړون په څرخېدو یو پر بل بدلېږي، کنفورمېشنل ایزومرونه بلل کېږي. خو هغه سټیریوایزومرونه چې د ځینو تړونونو له ماتولو او جوړولو پرته یو پر بل نه بدلېږي، کنفیګورېشنل ایزومرونه بلل کېږي. کنفورمېشنل ایزومېریزم د دې کتاب له چوکاټه بهر دی، نو یوازې کنفیګورېشنل ایزومېریزم څېړو، چې دوه ډوله دی: هندسي او نوري ایزومېریزم.

16.6.2.1 هندسي ایزومېریزم

کله چې په مالیکول کې څرخېدل محدود وي، هندسي ایزومرونه د اټومونو یا ګروپونو بېلابېل ترتیب لري. د بېلګې په توګه، بیوټ-2-ین دوه سټیریوایزومري بڼې لري: سیس-بیوټ-2-ین او ټرانس-بیوټ-2-ین، لکه لاندې چې ښودل شوي.

هغه ایزومر چې دواړه میتایل ګروپونه یې د دوه ګوني تړون پر یوه خوا وي، سیس (لاتیني کلمه، معنا یې “پر دې خوا”) ایزومر بلل کېږي، خو په ټرانس (لاتیني کلمه، معنا یې “بلې غاړې ته”) ایزومر کې دا ګروپونه د دوه ګوني تړون پر مخالفو خواوو وي. له همدې امله دا ډول ایزومېریزم سیس–ټرانس ایزومېریزم هم بلل کېږي. د کاربن–کاربن د دوه ګوني تړون د محدود څرخېدو له امله سیس او ټرانس ایزومرونه د پای تړون له ماتولو پرته یو پر بل نه بدلېږي. دا دوه بېلابېل مرکبات دي او بېلابېلې ځانګړنې لري.

په الکینونو کې هندسي ایزومېریزم یوازې هغه مهال ممکن دی چې د دوه ګوني تړون هر کاربني اټوم له دوو بېلابېلو اټومونو یا ګروپونو سره تړلی وي؛ نو پروپین هندسي ایزومرونه نه لري. په ځایناستو لرونکو سایکلوالکانونو کې هم هندسي ایزومېریزم ممکن دی. د بېلګې په توګه، 1،2-ډای میتایل سایکلوپروپان هم دوه هندسي ایزومرونه لري.

16.6.1.3 Functional group Isomerism

Functional group isomerism involves in compounds having the same formula but different functional groups. For example, ethyl alcohol and dimethyl ether are functional group isomers.

Similarly, Propionaldehyde and acetone are also functional group isomers.

16.6.1.4 Metamerism

This type of isomerism is exhibited due to the unequal distribution of carbon atoms (or alkyl groups) on either side of the functional group. Isomers belong to the same homologous series. For example, diethyl ether and methyl n-propyl ether are metamers.

16.6.1.5 Tautomerism

Tautomers are constitutional isomers that differ from each other by position of a proton (and may also a pi bond). It is a special type of functional group isomerism, in which the isomers are in dynamic equilibrium with each other. Tautomerization is the process of inter-conversion of tautomers, and an equilibrium process, which means that the equilibrium will establish with specific concentrations of tautomers of a compound. One of the important example of tautomerism is keto-enol tautomerism. The keto and enol tautomers of acetone are given below.

The result of this keto-enol tautomerization, is the migration of a proton from one location to another, accompanied by a change in location of the pi bond.

16.6.2 Stereoisomerism

When isomerism is caused by different arrangement of atoms or groups in space, the phenomenon is called stereoisomerism. Thus, the stereoisomers have the same molecular formula and connectivity of atoms, but differ in the arrangement of atoms or groups in space. In other words, the isomers that have the same constitution but differ in the spatial arrangement of their atoms are called stereoisomers. Some stereoisomers which are inter-convertible by rotation of single bond are called conformational isomers. But the stereoisomers which are not inter-convertible without breaking and making of some bonds, are called configurational isomers. Conformational isomerism is beyond the scope of this book, so we will discuss only the configurational isomerism in stereoisomers, which is of two types i.e. geometric and optical isomerism.

16.6.2.1 Geometrical Isomerism

Geometric isomers have different arrangement of atoms or groups when the rotation is restricted in a molecule. For example, but-2-ene have two stereoisomeric forms, cis-but-2-ene and trans-but-2-ene, as shown below.

The isomers in which the two methyl groups are on the same side of the double bond is called the cis (a Latin word meaning “on this side”) isomer, while trans (a Latin word meaning “across”) isomer has got them on the opposite sides of the double bond. Consequently this type of isomerism is also called cis-trans isomerism. Due to restricted rotation of carbon-carbon double bond, the cis and trans isomers are not inter-convertible without breaking of pi bond. These are two different compounds and have different properties.

Geometric isomerism in alkenes is possible only when each double bonded carbon atom is attached to two different atoms or groups, thus propene does not have geometric isomers. Geometric isomerism is also possible in substituted cycloalkanes. For example 1,2-dimethylcyclopropane also has two geometric isomers.
